Array Push Merge Behavior

Array Push Merge is a Merge behavior that combines array-based FeatureCell state values by pushing a single incoming value onto the existing array during the Merge stage.

This behavior treats arrays as immutable values. When the current state is an array and the incoming value is defined, the incoming value is appended as a single atomic element, producing a new array instance. The incoming value is never spread, flattened, or interpreted as a collection.

When the current value is not an array, the incoming value replaces the existing state directly. This ensures predictable structural behavior without attempting partial or mixed-type merging.

Array Push Merge runs within the core Merge stage and produces the merged candidate state passed to downstream pipeline stages. It does not mutate existing state, does not emit snapshots directly, and does not influence pipeline control flow beyond producing the merged value.

Note

The Merge stage is entered exclusively through explicit state-update APIs. Pipeline executions that invoke merge semantics are initiated via the mergeState method, which supply the incoming value and optional merge configuration used by the active Merge behavior.

Diagrams
Configuration

Array push merge behavior is configured as part of the Merge stage and defines how array-based FeatureCell state values are combined with incoming resolved values using single-element push semantics.

Exactly one merge behavior is active for a FeatureCell at any time. When withArrayPushMergeBehavior is provided, it replaces the default array replacement strategy and becomes the active merge behavior for that FeatureCell.

Merge behaviors may optionally be influenced by the clearUndefined configuration flag. When clearUndefined is enabled, an incoming undefined value is treated as an intentional clear request and results in the FeatureCell state being cleared. When disabled, incoming undefined values preserve the existing state and produce no merge output.

The clearUndefined option is supplied at the time a merge-style update is initiated and is evaluated by the active merge behavior during the Merge stage. It does not affect resolution, operators, or downstream pipeline stages.

Array push merge appends the incoming value as a single atomic element when the current state is an array. The incoming value is never spread, flattened, or interpreted as a collection. When the current value is not an array, the incoming value replaces the existing state directly.

Evaluation Outcomes

The Array Push Merge behavior evaluates the current committed FeatureCell state and the incoming resolved value to produce a single merged result during the Merge stage.

When the current state is an array, Array Push Merge appends the incoming value as a single atomic element and returns a new array. The incoming value is never spread, flattened, or interpreted as a collection.

When the current state is not an array, the incoming value replaces the existing state directly. No element-level reconciliation or mixed-type merging is performed.

When the incoming value is undefined, merge behavior is controlled by the clearUndefined configuration option. This determines whether the existing state is preserved or intentionally cleared.

Examples

Example 1: Use the withArrayPushMergeBehavior in a FeatureCell

This example demonstrates a FeatureCell configured with the withArrayPushMergeBehavior. Instead of replacing the existing array, incoming values provided via mergeState are appended to the current state, producing a new immutable array containing both existing and incoming entries.

By explicitly attaching the Array Push merge behavior, the FeatureCell adopts append-style semantics during the Merge stage, making it suitable for feed-style, log-style, or incremental list updates.

Note

When a custom merge behavior is supplied, it replaces the default withArrayMergeBehavior for that FeatureCell. Exactly one merge behavior is active at any time. 

{{`// app.config.ts

export const appConfig: ApplicationConfig = {
  providers: [
    provideVault({ logLevel: 'off' }),

    provideFeatureCell(
      EmployeeService
      {
        key: 'employees',
        initialState: []
      },
      [
        // Explicitly attach the Array Push merge behavior
        withArrayPushMergeBehavior
      ]
    )
  ]
};

// bank-employee.service.ts

import { Injectable } from '@angular/core';
import { FeatureCell, injectVault } from '@sdux-vault/angular';
import { Employee } from './employee.shape';

@FeatureCell`}}<Employee[]>{{`('employees')
@Injectable({ providedIn: 'root' })
export class EmployeeService {
  readonly vault = injectVault`}}<Employee[]>{{`(EmployeeService);

  constructor() {
    this.vault.initialize();
  }

  addEmployee(): void {
    this.vault.mergeState({
      value: [{ id: 1, name: 'Jane Doe' }]
    });
  }
}`}}
 
{{`export const employeeCell = FeatureCell`}}<Employee[]>{{`(
  {
    key: 'employees',
    initialState: [],
  },
  [
    // Explicitly attach the Array Push merge behavior
    withArrayPushMergeBehavior
  ]
);

// Initialize the FeatureCell
employeeCell.initialize();

// Push a new employee to existing state
employeeCell.mergeState({
  value: [{ id: 1, name: 'Jane Doe' }]
});`}}
